case_title: State of Maharashtra v. Abu Salem Abdul Kayyum Ansari and Ors.
neutral_facts: The case involves a murder committed by a group of individuals, with the victim being Pradeep Jain. The accused, including Abu Salem Abdul Kayyum Ansari, were involved in a conspiracy to murder the victim. The accused were tried for the murder, and the trial involved an accomplice who was granted conditional pardon under Section 307 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The accomplice was later found to have breached the conditions of his pardon, leading to a dispute over whether he could be cross-examined by the co-accused. The trial court allowed the co-accused to cross-examine the accomplice, but the State appealed this decision, arguing that the accomplice should no longer be considered a witness once his pardon was forfeited.
